title: The plural front-vowel class is too narrow
disclaimer: SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE. This language data was generated to demonstrate Motif. It is modelled loosely on Turkish, but it is not real Turkish, has not been checked by speakers, and must not be used as a description of any language.

symptom.reason: Motif shows 'No parse' for günler. The last vowel is ü, but -ler admits only e and i and -lar has the wrong vowel, so plural allomorph selection stops.

fix: Open the -ler alternate form for the plural entry in FieldWorks.
Set its environment to the Front class {e, i, ö, ü}, including the omitted rounded front vowels.
Save the project and refresh the Assessment.

title: Possessive and plural slots are reversed
disclaimer: SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE. This language data was generated to demonstrate Motif. It is modelled loosely on Turkish, but it is not real Turkish, has not been checked by speakers, and must not be used as a description of any language.

symptom.reason: Motif shows 'No parse' for adamlarında and okullarında. These cited forms require PL → POSS.3SG → LOC; reversing the Plural and Possessive slots leaves no path for that suffix sequence.

fix: Open the Noun affix template in FieldWorks.
Move the Plural slot before the Possessive slot; keep Case last.
Save the project and refresh the Assessment.

title: Vowel-final case forms omit the y linker
disclaimer: SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE. This language data was generated to demonstrate Motif. It is modelled loosely on Turkish, but it is not real Turkish, has not been checked by speakers, and must not be used as a description of any language.

symptom.reason: Motif shows 'No parse' for masaya, kediye, and kediyi. Each has y between a vowel-final noun and the case vowel; without vowel-final y allomorphs, no case form matches.

fix: Open the Dative and Accusative entries in FieldWorks.
Restore the vowel-final y forms (-ye/-ya and -yi/-yı/-yü/-yu) with environments for their final-vowel classes.
Save the project and refresh the Assessment.

title: Copied active templates slow noun parsing
disclaimer: SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE. This language data was generated to demonstrate Motif. It is modelled loosely on Turkish, but it is not real Turkish, has not been checked by speakers, and must not be used as a description of any language.

symptom.reason: Motif still parses these words, but Timing reports much more parser work. Sixteen equivalent active Noun templates give each noun sixteen routes through the same grammar.

fix: Open the Noun category's affix templates in FieldWorks.
Remove the duplicate active templates and keep one template with Plural, Possessive, and Case in order.
Save the project and refresh the Assessment.
